page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and there are no onboard GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests, while multi-core performance registers in the middle 50%. Memory performance is highly competitive, with large-block write bandwidth and Passmark memory scores reaching the top 10% tier. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds, alongside strong Passmark encryption test results.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is its minimal 1 GB network-attached local storage, which necessitates external storage solutions for data-heavy applications. However, its high memory bandwidth and strong single-core capabilities make it highly efficient for memory-intensive processing, static web serving, and Redis operations. It is also capable of executing small to medium LLM inference tasks, with text generation for 135M and 7B models achieving top-tier token-per-second throughput. This profile is well-suited for general-purpose application hosting, caching layers, and moderate computational workloads.
